Prevention: Grow strong smelling repelling plants like onion and garlic as border crops.
Cowpea and keep the field weed-free.
Conserving of natural enemies such as ladybird beetle, syrphids larvae, lace wing etc.
Use reflective mulches to repel invading populations of aphids.
Monitoring: Look at the leaves/stem for presence of ants, black shooty mold.
Monitor from germination up to maturity once per week.
Symptoms of infestation include crinkling and motteling of newly emerged leaf, the presence of a sticky stubstance on leaves and ant colonies.
If aphids are found on 2-3 plants per 20-30 then consider direct control actions.
If 4-10 pests are found per 20-30 plants then this is considered a severe infestation and chemical control is recommended.
Direct Control: Removal of affected twigs along with aphid colony at the early stage of growth.
Andrographis kashayam botanical products at a rate of 10 ml per litre.
Spraying of 1% Azadiractin at a rate of 300 ml per acre.
Spraying of water with high speed which will manage aphids in sticking with plants.
Destruction of ant colonies with flooding of water.
Restrictions: Always use protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label such as dosage, time of application.
Large quantities of pesticides will reduce natural enemies in the field.
RegentSC, Devigent plus, Fipro) at a rate of 300ml per acre.
Confidor, ltimo) at a rate of 60 ml per acre.
Actara, Anant, Renova, Evident, Spike, Click) at a rate of 50 g per acre.
